text:
alex: Heads-up — noticed a weird set of 'ghost' GPU nodepool partials in prod after the midnight autoscaler run. nodes show different labels than gitops state.

maria: ugh, can you paste the diff?

alex: quick snippet: 
```
# kubectl get nodes -l cloud.google.com/gke-nodepool -o json | jq '.items[] | {name: .metadata.name, labels: .metadata.labels}'
{
  "name": "gke-prod-gpu-0",
  "labels": {"env":"prod","gpu":"nvidia-a100","pool":"gpu-v2"}
}
{
  "name": "gke-prod-gpu-1",
  "labels": {"env":"prod","gpu":"nvidia-a100","pool":"gpu-canary"}
}
```
The gitops view (helm + kustomize overlay) expects pool: gpu-v2 for both.

simon: did the canary rollout complete? last night we merged the autoscaler change to allow burst pools.

jess: infra-bot reported a reconcile loop earlier: `gitops-operator reapply: manifest conflict: node-pool/gpu-canary`. Might be a timing window where autoscaler created nodes before helm reconciled.

maria: could be terraform vs gitops race — TF manages nodepool sizes, gitops manages nodepool labels via addon. We should check terraform state. alex, can you run `terraform state show module.nodepools.google_container_node_pool.gpu`?

alex: did that. state shows desired_size 4, actual 5 for gpu-v2, and there is a stray nodepool gpu-canary with size 1 in the project but not in our kustomize overlays.

simon: hmm — who ran a manual scale? any oncall activity?

jess: i queried audit logs: manual resize by service-account:ci-runner@redwood-inference-prod. That was from a CI job that retries scaling when a quota error occurs. CI attempted a temporary fallback to a canary pool `gpu-canary` in us-central1. It wasn't fully templatized so labels are wrong.

maria: that explains label divergence. Risk: scheduling difference and taint mismatch could send latency-sensitive pods to the wrong pool. Also cost spike — the canary pool uses older GPUs (higher per-hour).

alex: immediate mitigation: cordon the single gpu-canary node and drain non-critical workloads. Run: `kubectl cordon gke-prod-gpu-1 && kubectl drain gke-prod-gpu-1 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

simon: ack — I'll do cordon/drain now.

infra-bot: [automated alert] gitops-operator: manifest mismatch detected for nodepool/gpu-canary at 2026-11-08T03:04:12Z. Ticket #INF-912 queued.

simon: done cordon/drain, pods evicted. cpu/memory looked fine.

jess: created short-lived PR to add a guard in CI to prevent creating nodepools outside kustomize overlays: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4210 (will add an OPA check that blocks non-declared nodepools).

maria: sound good. parallel actions: (1) patch terraform to error on `var.allow_dynamic_nodepools=false` by default, (2) add a reconciler job to detect nodepools that exist in cloud but not in gitops and annotate them `reconcile=manual`.

alex: +1. Also scheduling a runbook step to alert cost-ops when an unexpected pool appears so we can freeze billing tags quickly.

simon: question on rollback: do we just delete gpu-canary pool after draining? or scale to zero then remove?

jess: scale to zero first to avoid immediate node deletion if something still lands there. Then remove resource through terraform plan/apply so state is correct.

maria: timeline: cordon/drain done (03:06). PR 4210 opened (03:09). I'm going to run a dry-run script to list any cloud-only nodepools across all regions and output to #eng-infra for review.

alex: posted dry-run results in channel: 2 extra pools in us-central1 and one in europe-west1. I'll open INF-913 for cleanup and attach terraform plan.

simon: cost note — that temporary pool added ~12 GPU-hours at a 30% premium because driver image is older and we had unnecessary preemption churn. Estimate ~$1.4k extra for the hour. tagging INF-914 for cost sync.

jess: ops checklist for next week: 1) add OPA gate in CI, 2) terraform var default to disallow dynamic pools, 3) reconcile detector job, 4) small playbook for oncall to cordon/drain + scale-zero + terraform remove. I'll convert to a draft runbook and ping @maria for review. :white_check_mark: 

maria: thanks all. follow-up: we should add a canary policy to the gitops operator that rejects nodepools without required labels (env, pool, gpu). That would have OPA coverage too.

alex: agreed. leaving this thread open until INF-913 shows cluster state cleaned and PR 4210 merged.

simon: closing steps: i'll create a short automation to notify oncall when terraform apply fails due to quota and block CI fallback. prevents future autocrated pools.

jess: nice catch, alex. :clap:

alex: thanks — will update INF-913 with commands used and the `kubectl` logs.

infra-bot: [ticket update] INF-912 -> assigned to jess at 1849991400.
